title: KV Cache Quantization for Diffusion Language Models
summary: The method replaces direct application of autoregressive KV cache quantizers (KIVI, KVQuant) to diffusion LLMs, where reused caches already diverge from full recomputation because bidirectional representations shift as masked tokens are revealed; it adds trajectory-based calibration (TRACE) and per-layer selective high-precision K-cache retention with low-bit value quantization. The cost is an offline calibration stage that must reconstruct feasible reveal trajectories from prompt-answer pairs, plus mixed-precision cache bookkeeping and per-layer selection logic. It can fail when production reveal schedules differ from the calibrated trajectories, when applied to dLLMs other than LLaDA/Dream, and it preserves only quality relative to other quantized baselines rather than eliminating the underlying cache-reuse error.
rationale: The technique is specific to diffusion language model inference, which the reader is unlikely to operate in production given constrained infrastructure and the limited maturity of dLLM deployments, so it merits monitoring rather than adoption.
technique: KV cache quantization for diffusion LLMs

The cost is an offline calibration stage that must reconstruct feasible reveal trajectories from prompt-answer pairs, plus mixed-precision cache bookkeeping and per-layer selection logic. It can fail when production reveal schedules differ from the calibrated trajectories, when applied to dLLMs other than LLaDA/Dream, and it preserves only quality relative to other quantized baselines rather than eliminating the underlying cache-reuse error.
dLLM-KVQ achieves the highest average score among quantized methods across 4-bit and 2-bit prefix/dual cache settings on LLaDA and Dream evaluated on GSM8K, HumanEval, MATH, and MBPP.
